subject: Critical Thinking
title: Status Quo Bias: The Devil You Know
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Status Quo Bias: The Devil You Know.

hook.text: When organ donation is opt-in, participation is ~15%. When it's opt-out, it's ~90%. Same choice. Different default.

buildup.text: Status quo bias: people overwhelmingly prefer the current state of affairs, even when change is objectively better.

discovery.text: It combines loss aversion (change risks loss), endowment effect (we overvalue what we have), and effort avoidance.

twist.text: Governments and companies weaponize this. Auto-enrolled subscriptions, pre-checked boxes — defaults control behavior.

climax.text: The most powerful policy tool isn't incentives or laws — it's choosing what the default option is.

punchline.text: The default wins. Whoever sets it controls the outcome.

quiz.question: Why does organ donation skyrocket when it's opt-out instead of opt-in?
options: Status quo bias makes people stick with the default
Opt-out forms are easier to read

details.summary: Status quo bias is the preference for the current state of affairs even when change would be beneficial. It combines loss aversion, inertia, and fear of the unknown into a powerful resistance to improvement.
details.whyItMatters: Status quo bias keeps people in suboptimal defaults for everything from retirement plans to career paths, costing them opportunities they never seriously evaluate.
takeaways: Default options have enormous power because of status quo bias
The bias combines loss aversion with simple inertia
Opt-out systems exploit status quo bias for good or ill

faq.question: How do companies exploit status quo bias with default settings?
faq.answer: Subscription services default to auto-renewal, phone apps default to maximum data sharing, and retirement plans default to conservative investments. Most people never change defaults, so the chosen default shapes outcomes.

faq.question: How can awareness of status quo bias help you make better choices?
faq.answer: Periodically audit your defaults by asking: would I actively choose this option if I were starting from scratch today? If the answer is no, the status quo is holding you back.
